rows.citation: Ling, X., Menzies, T. (2023). What Not to Test (For Cyber-Physical Systems). IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 49(7), 3811-3826.
rows.model_type: Simulink cyber-physical simulation models (six case studies with mutants reused from Arrieta et al.)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - reuses generated Simulink mutants (arithmetic, logical, relational, connection operators) to judge whether selected tests distinguish mutants from the original.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - test cases are distinct input signals simulated on each model; selection chooses among many candidate test inputs.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - no electrophysiology; uses signal-derived goals (output discontinuity, instability, growth to infinity, variance) as a domain feature analogue.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - DoLesS picks a minimal effective test subset via least-squares approximation over multiple goals; compares to NSGA-II-based prior selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - evaluation repeats runs on the same case studies; no held-out models or held-out mutation families found in the arXiv text.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI or coding-agent edits; mutants are rule-based.
rows.software: DoLesS reproduction package, https://github.com/ai-se/DoLesS (GitHub API reports no license)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest structural analogue in CPS: mutation-guided minimal test selection over simulated signals. NeuroSem adds conductance neuron models, eFEL features, refinement-calibrated tolerances, admissibility classification, held-out models and mutation family, random cost-matched baselines.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar API (abstract, arXiv 2112.01598 link); arXiv abs page and full-text PDF read; GitHub REST API for repository.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:dl.acm.org test selection simulation models cyber-physical Simulink mutation; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Zhang, J., Ghobari, D., Sabetzadeh, M., et al. (2025). Simulink Mutation Testing using CodeBERT. 2025 IEEE/ACM International Conference on Automation of Software Test (AST), 24-28.
rows.model_type: Simulink / Stateflow models (Lockheed Martin benchmark plus FIM tool examples)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - generates compilable Simulink mutants by masking model-text tokens and substituting CodeBERT predictions; compares against rule-based FIM mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - mutants are exercised by test cases from a reference test suite per model; stimuli are not designed or varied systematically.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - kill criteria are output differences (classical) or requirement violations (requirements-aware), not biophysical features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - selects a minimal test subset killing each tool's mutants, but only as an instrument for comparing mutant generators.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - tests selected using one generator's mutants are scored on the other generator's mutants (cross-family), but no held-out models.
rows.ai_transformations: partial - a fine-tuned language model generates the faults; no evaluation of AI coding agents editing models.
rows.software: none (no code or data link found in arXiv 2501.07553 full text)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Focuses on learned mutant generation for block diagrams. NeuroSem uses curated single-fault NeuroML/LEMS operators, stimulus-protocol selection, feature tolerances and held-out models; cross-generator test transfer is a useful design precedent.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, pages); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar API (abstract, arXiv id); arXiv abs page and full-text PDF read.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:dl.acm.org mutation analysis Simulink models signal features (arXiv 2501.07553 link); verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Palomo-Lozano, F., Estero-Botaro, A., Medina-Bulo, I., et al. (2018). Test suite minimization for mutation testing of WS-BPEL compositions. Proceedings of the Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference (GECCO '18), 1427-1434.
rows.model_type: WS-BPEL web-service compositions (general software, not simulation models)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - minimization constraint is preserving mutation coverage of the compositions; mutant generation details not read (full text closed).
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - existing test cases act as candidate inputs; no stimulus design.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - kill decisions are software output differences.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - exact Integer Linear Programming minimization of the test suite subject to unchanged mutation coverage, motivated by costly executions.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract reports no held-out compositions or mutant families; full text not accessible.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Provides an exact alternative to greedy coverage selection on a mutant-by-test matrix. NeuroSem applies selection to neuron stimulation protocols under a budget and tests generalization to held-out models and mutation families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata, pages); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar API (abstract; S2 lists open access as closed).
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:dl.acm.org test suite minimization greedy set cover mutation; verified via Crossref

rows.citation: Goyal, A., Shyamasundar, R.K., Sivakumar, G., et al. (2021). Empirical Analysis of Greedy, GE and GRE Heuristics. Proceedings of the 14th Innovations in Software Engineering Conference (ISEC 2021), 1-11.
rows.model_type: general software regression test suites (synthetic requirement-coverage matrices)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - coverage is of requirements, modelled as normally distributed per test; no mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - abstract test cases only; no stimulus concept.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - compares Greedy, Greedy Essential and GRE minimization heuristics by output size and runtime across overlap ratios.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - empirical study on generated instances; no held-out generalization question.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Background only for the greedy set-cover step, which NeuroSem does not claim as novel. NeuroSem's contribution lies in the neuroscience mutant/protocol/feature construction and held-out evaluation, not the heuristic.
rows.verification_method: Crossref works API (metadata); OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar API (abstract).

rows.citation: Troya, J., Segura, S., Burgueño, L., et al. (2022). Model Transformation Testing and Debugging: A Survey. ACM Computing Surveys 55(4), 1-39.
rows.model_type: survey of model-driven engineering model transformations (140 papers)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - abstract does not state mutation coverage; survey body not read (paywalled).
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - concerns transformation input models, not stimuli to dynamical simulations.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - test generation surveyed per abstract; test selection or minimization coverage not verified.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - survey; no evaluation of its own.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Taxonomy background for testing transformations (relevant to NeuroML/LEMS translation). NeuroSem judges behavioural preservation through simulated electrophysiology across protocols rather than structural or oracle checks on transformed models.

rows.citation: Shelburg, J., Kessentini, M., Tauritz, D.R. (2013). Regression Testing for Model Transformations: A Multi-objective Approach. Search Based Software Engineering (SSBSE 2013), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, 209-223.
rows.model_type: MDE metamodels and model transformation rules
rows.controlled_mutations: no - reacts to real metamodel changes; no mutants described in abstract.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - multiple test case models serve as transformation inputs; no dynamical stimuli.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - metamodel coverage and validity, not behavioural features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - multi-objective search refactors existing test models to maximize new-metamodel coverage while minimizing refactorings and invalid elements.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - validated on one widely used transformation; no held-out split.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares the re-test-after-evolution motivation only. NeuroSem targets semantic drift in simulated neuron behaviour, using fault injection, stimulus batteries and calibrated feature tolerances rather than structural coverage.
